# yottabot_mcp_gateway (Resource)

A registered MCP gateway — a routeable endpoint the platform can call. This is catalog configuration only: deploying the MCP server itself belongs in your infra modules.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "yottabot_mcp_gateway" "github" {
  name        = "github-mcp"
  description = "Routes MCP tool calls to the GitHub MCP server."
  endpoint    = "https://mcp.example.com/github"
  transport   = "streamable_http"
  status      = "available"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `endpoint` (String) Gateway URL the platform calls.
- `name` (String) Gateway name.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Free-text description.
- `status` (String) Lifecycle status: `draft`, `available` (default), `unavailable`, or `deprecated`. This is registry lifecycle, **not** operational health — see `health_status`.
- `transport` (String) `streamable-http` (default), `stdio`, or `sse`.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp.
- `created_by_user_id` (String) Creator's user UUID.
- `health_status` (String) Operational health of deployed instances (`healthy`/`degraded`/`down`/`unknown`). Computed and deliberately separate from `status`: one registered gateway can have several live instances.
- `id` (String) Server-assigned UUID. This is the import id.
- `modified_at` (String) Last modification timestamp.
- `tools_count` (Number) Number of tools the gateway exposes.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import yottabot_mcp_gateway.github b41d7e02-5c68-4a39-8d1b-7e3f9a0c6d52
```
